fields.label: Tension Title
fields.name: tension_title
fields.default_value: The mandate landed. The pacing guide didn’t move.

fields.label: Paragraph 1
fields.name: tension_p1
fields.default_value: You’ve been handed a district-wide literacy initiative. Your Social Studies teachers have a curriculum map that waits for no one. And somewhere in the middle, students are being asked to read like historians without ever being taught how.

fields.label: Paragraph 2 (Bold)
fields.name: tension_p2
fields.default_value: This is the gap Dr. Miles closes.

fields.label: Paragraph 3
fields.name: tension_p3
fields.default_value: Not with generic reading strategies stapled onto your existing units. Not with a two-day PD that disappears by Monday. But with job-embedded coaching that meets your teachers where they are — inside their planning time, inside their content, inside their classrooms.

fields.label: Title
fields.name: distinction_title
fields.default_value: There’s a difference. Most PD doesn’t know it.

fields.label: Highlight Paragraph 1
fields.name: distinction_highlight_p1
fields.default_value: Most literacy professional development teaches adolescent literacy — foundational strategies for accessing complex text.

fields.label: Highlight Paragraph 2 (Bold)
fields.name: distinction_highlight_p2
fields.default_value: Dr. Miles teaches disciplinary literacy — the specialized practice of reading, writing, and thinking like a historian.

fields.label: Callout Box Paragraph 1
fields.name: distinction_callout_p1
fields.default_value: That distinction changes everything. A student who can identify the main idea of a passage is not the same as a student who can source a primary document, contextualize an era, and corroborate competing accounts.

fields.label: Callout Box Paragraph 2
fields.name: distinction_callout_p2
fields.default_value: The second student is college-ready. The second student is what Social Studies was always meant to produce.

fields.label: Callout Box Paragraph 3 (Gold)
fields.name: distinction_callout_p3
fields.default_value: ICLS exists to get your department there.

fields.label: Title
fields.name: approach_title
fields.default_value: We go where the work actually happens.

fields.label: Paragraph 1
fields.name: approach_p1
fields.default_value: Every ICLS engagement is built around one principle: real change happens in collaborative planning rooms, not conference centers.

fields.label: Paragraph 2
fields.name: approach_p2
fields.default_value: Dr. Miles embeds directly into your teachers’ professional learning communities — bringing targeted historical inquiry routines into the spaces where your team already works together. No extra sessions to schedule. No separate literacy block to carve out. The content is the literacy.

fields.label: Paragraph 3
fields.name: approach_p3
fields.default_value: When teachers feel genuinely supported — not managed, not mandated — they build the confidence to lead students deeper. That’s where student growth becomes measurable.

fields.label: Heading
fields.name: bio_heading
fields.default_value: Twenty years in the room. Now she’s in yours.

fields.label: Paragraph 1
fields.name: bio_text1
fields.default_value: Dr. Kimberly Nicole Miles built ICLS from the inside out — starting in elementary classrooms, moving through secondary and collegiate instruction, and spending two decades watching what happens when literacy is treated as an English teacher’s problem instead of everyone’s responsibility.

fields.label: Paragraph 2
fields.name: bio_text2
fields.default_value: She holds an Ed.D. with professional endorsements in Instructional Coaching, Gifted Education, ESOL, and Math (K–5). Her peer-reviewed research on adolescent disciplinary literacy in Georgia’s Social Studies classrooms has been recognized as a benchmark regional framework for secondary integration.

fields.label: Italic Text
fields.name: bio_italic_text
fields.default_value: She doesn’t just study this. She’s lived it.
